wiki.content: “Lost Boys” is the first single from Phoebe Bridgers' third studio album, Lost Weekend. Phoebe unveiled the song on May 8, 2026, at The Liberty in Roswell, New Mexico. As her first solo performance in nearly three years, it was the kickoff show for a pop-up tour across the U.S., during which she played "Lost Boys" as well as other new songs from Lost Weekend. Bridgers is joined by a number of special guests on “Lost Boys,” including Julien Baker, Lucy Dacus, and Caroline Shaw on vocals; Alex G on drums and voice memo; Jack Antonoff on electric guitar, synths, drums, and vocoder; Bright Eyes’ Nate Walcott on trumpets; Blake Mills on synths; Chris Thile on mandolin; and Christian Lee Hutson on acoustic guitar, among others. The song was produced by Bridgers, Tony Berg, Ethan Gruska, and Antonoff, and features additional production by Alex G. The verses contrast a world where chaos, fantasy, and fleeting intimacy become shields against the ache of "real" adulthood. Bridgers seems to be singing about people who have ditched the capitalist rat race and its everyday hell, choosing instead a life of wandering and self-discovery. They live like nomads, dodging the usual "adult milestones". It’s a Neverland fantasy where life isn’t about bills or boring jobs, but about something looser, freer, and more alive. The music video, which dropped alongside the single on June 25, 2026, brings that vision into even clearer and more striking focus. Read more on Last.fm.
